content.text:
I've set up the Go module in `/work` with a reusable diff package and a small command-line tool. Vet passes, the tests pass, and running it on sample files gives correct output.

**Layout**
```
go.mod                  module difftool (go 1.27.1)
diff/diff.go            the diff package
diff/diff_test.go       tests
cmd/difftool/main.go    the command
.gitignore              ignores the built binary
```

**Dependency:** I used `github.com/aymanbagabas/go-udiff` v0.4.1 to compute the diff instead of writing my own. It's a maintained copy of the diff code inside the Go tools (`golang.org/x/tools/internal/diff`). I didn't use `pmezard/go-difflib` because it was archived in 2018. One thing to know: the library's `ApplyUnified` (which applies a diff back to text) only works on diffs with no context lines. My first test used it and failed for that reason, so I replaced that test with one for a missing final newline.

**Package API (`difftool/diff`)**
- `Unified(oldLabel, newLabel, old, new string, context int) string` returns a standard unified diff with `---`/`+++`/`@@` lines. It returns `""` when the inputs are equal, so tests can use `if d := diff.Unified(...); d != "" { t.Errorf(...) }`. A negative `context` means the default of 3 lines. It also marks a missing final newline with `\ No newline at end of file`.
- `Colorize(unified string) string` adds terminal colors: red for `-` lines, green for `+`, cyan for `@@`, bold for the headers.

**Command**
```
go run ./cmd/difftool [-U n] [-color] OLD NEW
```
Either input can be `-` to read from stdin. Like `diff(1)`, it exits 0 when the files are the same, 1 when they differ, and 2 on an error.

I haven't made a commit; there are no commits on `master` yet. The module path is the placeholder `difftool`. If this will be imported from another repo, rename it to the real repo path (e.g. `github.com/you/difftool`) in `go.mod` and in the import in `cmd/difftool/main.go`.
